summary: Dune: Imperium – Uprising is a standalone expansion/sequel that keeps the same worker-placement-plus-deckbuilding core but adds new mechanisms like sandworm riding, spy networks, and contracts for extra strategic texture. It supports up to 6 players with a new team mode, making it feel like a bigger, richer version of the original rather than a wholly new game.
praised: Adds meaningful new strategic layers (spies, sandworms, contracts) without bloating the core
Compatible with base game and other expansions for mix-and-match variety
criticised: Slightly higher complexity and longer setup than the base game
Some new mechanics can feel like they dilute the tight original design
Best experienced after already knowing the base game
Team mode can be uneven depending on group experience

interaction.kind: bumping opponents off shared spaces, Conflict-track fights, and (in 6p mode) team-based opposition
interaction.detail: Shared worker-placement spots and the Conflict track remain the main friction points, now joined by sandworm riding and spy interactions that can target opponents. Most of a turn is still personal deck/tableau development, with the team variant adding a more overtly adversarial layer.
interaction.said: Reviewers describe it the same way as base Imperium — bumping opponents from spaces and fighting over Conflict — with the added team mode making cooperation/opposition even more explicit ('two-team struggle')

subsystems: Combat/Conflict track (troop strength, garrison, leader combat bonuses)
Faction influence & alliances (four factions, each with its own influence track)
Imperium Row card economy (Technology tiles, Intrigue cards, Spice Must Flow cards)
sources: Faction alliance tokens (per faction reaching Ally status)
Spice Must Flow cards (converted to VP via endgame Intrigue cards)
scoring.how_you_win: Players build a deck/worker-placement engine to win conflicts, ally with factions, and accumulate cards that grant Victory Points on a shared, publicly visible track; once any player reaches 10+ VP (or the Conflict Deck runs out), the current round finishes and whoever has the most VP wins, with spice, solari, water, and troops as tiebreakers.
